card: This PR subtracts the gossip time penalty from an incoming address's timestamp when AddrMan evaluates whether the announcement contains newer information than what is already stored. Currently, because stored entries have a 2-hour penalty applied on insertion, comparing unpenalized incoming timestamps against stored penalized timestamps causes identical gossip announcements from different peers to appear newer than the existing record. This circumvents the intended check and allows a single broadcast to artificially increase an address's multiplicity in the new table up to 8. The author notes this is a logic bugfix for benign multi-path relay rather than an adversarial defense, as an attacker could still intentionally send increments to nTime.
evidence: PR description: "However, the check is ineffective: when the entry was first added, its nTime was stored with a 2h time penalty applied, so addr.nTime > pinfo->nTime holds even for an identical announcement. As a result, a single announcement relayed to us by several peers could increase an address's multiplicity in the new table, up to 8."

Author clarifies limitation in PR description: "This is just a small logic bugfix, it doesn't change things in adversarial scenarios, since peers can just do multiple announcements with changed nTime if they want to boost their RefCount artificially."
problem: When an address entry is first stored in AddrMan, a time penalty (typically 2 hours) is subtracted from its timestamp. When the identical announcement arrives from other gossip relay peers, AddrMan compares the raw announcement timestamp against the stored penalized timestamp without adjusting for the penalty, causing the check to falsely conclude that newer information arrived and inflating the address's multiplicity up to 8.
summary: Subtracts the applicable time penalty from an address's timestamp when checking whether an incoming address announcement contains new information in AddrMan. This prevents identical announcements relayed across multiple peers from mistakenly passing the timestamp freshness check and increasing the address's multiplicity in the "new" table.
